area: hygiene: public distribution hygiene of the frozen release build (test-results/audit/build/release.html, version 2.1.0) and of the repository as it would be published
summary: The shipped file is clean on its own terms: no secrets, no personal data, no test hooks, no console output, and not one request beyond the document itself in 9 played weeks plus all 25 named states. Six things need a decision: the fiction and non-affiliation statement the brief asks for is absent from the game; the announcer prefers online speech voices in Chrome and Edge; two tracked documents name five people; the file handed on by itself lacks one copyright notice and every licence text; the game has no licence of its own; and the notices file omits one bundled package by name.
verified_ok: The audited file is the tracked release: test-results/audit/build/release.html, Tech_Sales_Trail_2.1.html and index.html share sha256 5c495f11...406dae0e (559,646 bytes). The working tree is clean after the audit; everything I wrote is under test-results/audit/hygiene/.

(1) Secrets: 20 credential patterns (AWS, GitHub, Slack, Google, OpenAI/Anthropic, Stripe and npm tokens, private-key blocks, JWTs, bearer and basic-auth URLs, key/secret/password assignments, DSNs, analytics IDs) over the frozen build and all 394 tracked files: 0 hits. The core patterns over the file contents of all 133 revisions: 0 hits. By eye, every 'token', 'secret' or 'password' in tracked text is game copy ('token true-up', 'You have typed the password correctly on the fourth try'). No .env, .npmrc or key file is tracked. package-lock.json resolves all 57 packages from registry.npmjs.org.

(2) Personal information in the distributable: none. No e-mail address, path, hostname, username, author credit or version number appears on screen or in the file. The only HTML comment is the notices header; there are no source paths, source maps or licence banners. The three embedded fonts are byte-identical to src/assets/fonts and their name tables hold only upstream data (Inter Project Authors and JetBrains Mono Project Authors copyright lines, licence URLs, vendor IDs RSMS and JB). The icon sprite is 56 symbols identical to lucide-static 1.70.0 with no metadata.

(2) Names a player sees: the character is 'Matt' (src/copy/ui.js:10, src/copy/memo.js:8 'Welcome to Shitcorp, Matt!', the scene ping '@matt') and the employer is 'Shitcorp' (ui.js:9). No author credit exists anywhere a player can look (boot screen, memo, handbook, settings menu, endings).

(2) Repository: package.json has no author, repository, homepage or licence field ('private': true). No e-mail address occurs in the contents of any revision. The only absolute path is the generic /home/user/tech-sales-trail (9 lines in 5 files under qa/2.1/evidence/). The 58 tracked pictures (54 JPG, 4 WebP) carry JFIF and ICC data only, no EXIF, XMP or comments; I looked at screenshots/main.webp and it is page content only. README.md:5 and :22 carry the owner's GitHub handle in the play link, which is intended.

(3) Customer names: none of the 57 account names in src/copy/names.js is a real company's name. The closest resemblances are whimsical compounds on ordinary or coined words: 'Cronut Cloud' (Cronut is a bakery's registered trade mark), 'Pinecone Pizza', 'Infinite Wasabi' and 'Neon Narwhal' (each first or second word is also a real tech vendor's name), 'Kintsugi Metrics', 'Obsidian Harbor', 'Polaris Tacos', 'Signal Pagoda'. The copy says nothing factual about any of them. The team already renamed 'Oracle Dumpling' in 2.0 (CHANGELOG.md:156); it survives only in the frozen test baseline test/baseline/v1.21/index.html. Renaming more would change stored saves, golden replays and README pictures for no player benefit: leave them.

(3) Brand-like names in the copy: 'ChatGDP' is parody, the manager's misnomer (docs/2.1/TTST_2.1_Editorial_Copydeck.md:7); 'ChatGPT' occurs 0 times in the build. 'Fortune 500,000 company' is a joke made on the owner's instruction (CHANGELOG.md:44). 'SOC 2 Type II' and 'SSO' are badges on the parody ad. Shitcorp, Scheisskorp and clAInk are invented. Two real product names reach the player, both deliberate: 'Slack' twice in one clAInk outcome line (src/copy/claink.js:35, approved at copydeck line 423 and on the lint allowlist) and 'Post-it' in the Ascension scene's text summary (src/copy/scenes.js:69). 'Google ...' and 'Microsoft ...' occur only as browser voice identifiers in code, never on screen.

(4) Test hooks: the release script (405,460 characters) contains 0 '__TST', no TST_CLAINK or TST_DEV, no 'debugger', and none of the seed, dice or cosmetic-roll hooks the test build has (__TST_SEED, __TST_RNG, __TST_FX, __TST_STRAYS, TST_CLAINK). The three globals it does set are the game's own plumbing between modules, with the test-only members compiled out: TST_AUDIO (play, say, cancelSay, hush, ambient, stopAmbient, setStress, onLogs, onModal, setOn, setVoice, setVolume, setCaptions, unlock, settings, onChange, onCaption), TST_SCENES (play, reduced, summaryFor, COLS, ROWS) and TST_TOAST. No URL parameter or hidden key changes anything (keys: 1-9, 0, -, =, E, H, ?, M, Esc).

(5) Network, read from the file: the only http(s) URLs are the 5 in the header comment. Thirteen escaped strings in React are identifiers nothing fetches (w3.org namespaces, the reactjs.org error-decoder prefix). There is no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon, dynamic import, Worker, service worker, Image(), Audio(), window.open or cookie use. There is no script src, img, iframe, a, form, base, meta refresh, preload or manifest; the one link is the data: favicon. The CSS has three url() values, all data:font/woff2, and no @import. Sound effects are Web Audio synthesis with no audio files.

(5) Network, observed in Chromium with every request logged and refused: as a new player from file:// (boot, memo, tour, handbook, settings, the clAInk ad, 4 weeks, 15 actions) and from a made-up http origin (5 weeks, 20 actions) the page made 1 request, the document, plus 3 data: font loads. Opened on each of the 25 named states (six endings with their cutscenes, clAInk runs and reports): 0 requests beyond the document. No websocket, popup, worker, frame or download; 0 cookies. Storage is localStorage tst-onboarded-v2 and tst-autosave-v5 and sessionStorage tst-booted; the save envelope holds only app, schemaVersion, build, savedAt, the dice state and the run. Logs: test-results/audit/hygiene/session-file.json and session-http.json.

(7) Diagnostics: 0 console messages of any type and 0 page errors in all of those sessions. The file has five console.error call sites, all on error paths (four inside React and its scheduler, one in the game's error boundary at src/ui/main.jsx:16), and no console.log, debug, info or warn. The one alert() is the fallback of the toast (src/ui/env.js:6).

(6) Links: none is shown to the player (0 anchors in the page in every state visited). In the file's header comment, unverified but well-formed: https://github.com/rsms/inter, https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono, https://opensource.org/license/mit, https://opensource.org/license/isc-license-txt, https://openfontlicense.org. README.md: the owner's GitHub Pages play link (twice), two img.shields.io badge images (the second has an unescaped middle dot that renderers percent-encode), https://react.dev, https://rsms.me/inter/, https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/, https://lucide.dev. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md: the two GitHub URLs, http://scripts.sil.org/OFL and https://scripts.sil.org/OFL (verbatim from the licence texts). docs/DEVELOPMENT.md: https://playwright.dev. None is malformed. All 21 relative links and heading anchors in the 10 tracked Markdown files resolve.

(8) Notices against the bundle: the file's header names exactly what is bundled (react 18.3.1, react-dom 18.3.1, scheduler 0.23.2, Inter 4.001 and JetBrains Mono 2.211 as subsets, Lucide 1.70.0 with 56 icons). The source imports only react and react-dom/client. The build tools (esbuild, @babel/standalone, fontkit, subset-font) and any analytics or telemetry library are absent from the script. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md matches node_modules ('node scripts/notices.mjs --check' reports it up to date). MIT, ISC and OFL 1.1 all permit redistribution, the fonts are embedded and not sold alone, and neither font declares a Reserved Font Name.

findings.title: The game carries no fiction or non-affiliation statement; the only one is the last line of the README, and it says neither 'independent' nor 'unaffiliated'
findings.where: src/copy/help.js (HELP, lines 27-57: the handbook has no About section); on screen: 'How it works'; README.md:257
findings.evidence: Searching all 1,928 player strings and the built file for fiction, satir, parod, affiliat, endors, resembl, coinciden, disclaim, trademark and independent finds only unrelated lines ('Self-authored legal disclaimers.', 'Revenue verified independently of clAInk.', 'the funnel resembles a funnel') and React's copyright line. On screen the handbook has five sections (The quarter, The funnel, You, The office, Keyboard) and a footer with 'Read the memo again' and 'Got it'; the settings menu has Sound, Office announcer, Captions for the announcer, Volume, Save run, Load saved run, New run. There is no About area, version or credit anywhere (pictures: test-results/audit/hygiene/session-file-04-handbook.png, handbook-1366-scrolled.png, handbook-390-bottom.png, session-file-05-settings.png). README.md:257 reads: '*Tech Sales Trail is satire. Shitcorp, Scheisskorp, clAInk and every customer in the game are made up. Any resemblance to your actual quarter is a coincidence, and we are sorry.*' That states fiction but not independence or non-affiliation, and it does not travel with the file (README.md:23: 'That one file is the whole game').
findings.proposal: In src/copy/help.js, append one entry to HELP after the Keyboard entry (lines 54-56): { title: "About", rows: [{ term: "Tech Sales Trail", body: () => " is an independently developed fictional satire of the technology sales industry. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any employer or technology vendor." }] }. The row format (bold term, then body) renders the studio's sentence word for word with the game's name in bold, and src/ui/Game.jsx:275-280 needs no change. On screen it is the last block of the right-hand column of 'How it works' on a desktop, under Keyboard, and the last paragraph above the footer on a phone, where Keyboard is hidden. Optional: add the second sentence to README.md:257.
findings.risk: The handbook grows by a heading and two or three lines. At widths above 1024px the two-column balance may move a paragraph across the column break; the dialog already scrolls at 1366x768 (content 847px in 742px), so the new block is reached by scrolling there. The handbook pictures in qa/2.1/screenshots and the 'handbook' state of test/e2e/matrix.cjs need re-running. The entry must not carry keys: true or it disappears on touch screens. The copy lint already allows 'Tech Sales Trail'; lint.params and test/engine/copy.test.mjs:77 walk HELP generically; copy coverage checks deck to game only, so a line outside the copydeck does not fail it.

findings.title: In Chrome and Edge the announcer picks an online speech voice over the local ones, so its lines are synthesized by Google's or Microsoft's service
findings.where: src/engine/audio/voice.js:20-21 (VOICE_PREFS) and :31-32 (the ranking); the claims at README.md:23, README.md:220 and CHANGELOG.md:321
findings.evidence: voice.js:31 ranks a voice as 'i*2 + (v.localService === false ? 1 : 0)', so an online voice loses only to a local voice with the same name prefix; the lists start with 'Google UK English Male' (announcer) and 'Microsoft Aria' (HR). I ran the release build with speechSynthesis replaced by a recorder and the voice lists desktop browsers report (test-results/audit/hygiene/voices.cjs). Chrome on Windows: the announcer's 'Quota assigned. Good morning.' went to 'Google UK English Male' (localService=false) although local Microsoft David and Mark were offered. Chrome on macOS: announcer to Google UK English Male and HR to Google UK English Female, both online, although local Daniel and Samantha were offered. Edge on Windows: 'Microsoft Guy Online (Natural)' and 'Microsoft Aria Online (Natural)' although local David and Zira were offered. Firefox and Safari lists (local voices only) got local voices. This contradicts voice.js:17 ('they need the network, so a local voice of the same family wins'), CHANGELOG.md:321 ('local voices win over Edge's "Online (Natural)" ones'), README.md:23 ('It loads nothing from anywhere'), README.md:220 ('Sound is synthesized in the page: effects, a heartbeat when stress runs hot, and the office PA') and the file's header ('it makes no network requests'). Sound and 'Office announcer' are on by default. What would leave the machine is the text of the canned lines in src/copy/pa.js, never player data. The page itself made 0 requests in every session. Not observed: the browser's own traffic, because this Chromium reports 0 voices; that online voices are synthesized remotely is documented browser behaviour, and the voice lists are my reconstruction of what those browsers report. test/audio/lib/fakes.mjs:37 marks 'Google UK English Male' as localService: true, so the suite never meets the real flag. Offline, voice.js:68-72 retries once on the browser's default voice and captions carry every line.
findings.proposal: Two lines in pickVoice (voice.js:31-32): let online-ness outrank list position, for example 'var online = v.localService === false ? 100 : 0;' then 'rank = online + i' for a listed voice and 'rank = online + 50' for the English fallback. An online voice is then used only where the browser offers no local English voice. If the owner prefers how the online voices sound, leave the code and correct README.md:23 and :220 instead: the announcer uses the browser's speech voices, which in Chrome and Edge can be online ones, and turning 'Office announcer' off keeps everything local.
findings.risk: The announcer sounds different to Chrome and Edge players: an operating-system voice such as Microsoft David or Daniel instead of Google UK English Male or Edge's Natural voices, which is audibly plainer. Chrome on Linux and ChromeOS, where only online voices exist, is unchanged. The audio tests (test/audio/behaviour.test.mjs:98, 103-104) keep passing because their fake voices are all local. No rule, save or layout is touched; the release file's bytes change.

findings.title: Two tracked documents name five people with job titles
findings.evidence: Implementation.md:3 reads '**From:** [name], Creative Director; [name], Engineering; [name], Production; [name], Art; [name], Editorial'. Copydeck.md:2 reads '**[name] | Editorial | Operation Final Coat**'. A search of every tracked file finds these names nowhere else, and none is in the built file. Both lines are present in 30 revisions of each document. I cannot tell whether these are real people or personas. Either way, a public reader sees a five-person staff with titles behind a game the new statement will call 'independently developed', and if they are real it is third-party personal information of the kind the brief asks to remove.
findings.proposal: The owner confirms what the names are. If they are real people, or the project is to be presented as one person's, replace the two attribution lines with roles only, for example 'From: creative direction, engineering, production, art, editorial' and 'Editorial | Operation Final Coat'. That is two lines in two documents; no tool reads them.
findings.risk: None to the game or its checks: scripts/copy-coverage.mjs reads the copydeck's table rows, not its header lines. The names remain in git history unless the history is rewritten, which is outside this pass.

findings.title: Handed on by itself, the game file lacks one copyright notice (Feather, for 10 of its 56 icons) and every licence text
findings.where: scripts/build.mjs:99-140 (notices(), which writes the header comment); lines 1-10 of test-results/audit/build/release.html
findings.evidence: The header gives four copyright lines (React, Inter, JetBrains Mono, Lucide) and 'Licence texts: https://opensource.org/license/mit, https://opensource.org/license/isc-license-txt and https://openfontlicense.org'. In the file, 'Permission is hereby granted', 'Permission to use, copy', 'SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE' and 'Cole Bemis' each occur 0 times. Ten of the 56 bundled icons (arrow-right, calendar, check, compass, info, loader, lock, minus, search, x; compass is also the favicon and the wordmark) are on the 'derived from the Feather project' list in node_modules/lucide-static/LICENSE, which puts them under MIT with 'Copyright (c) 2013-present Cole Bemis'. MIT and ISC ask that the copyright notice and the permission notice appear in all copies; the OFL asks that each copy contain the notice and the licence. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md has all of it, including the Feather notice, but README.md:23 tells players to take index.html alone, and the links need the network the game otherwise never uses.
findings.proposal: (a) One line in notices() after build.mjs:127 crediting Feather for the bundled icons on that list ('10 of them derived from Feather. Copyright (c) 2013-present Cole Bemis. MIT License.'), computed from the same LICENSE the build already reads. It fits: the charset check stands at 823 of 1024 bytes. (b) The owner's call: also carry the texts in the file, as a second comment after the closing html tag generated from the three licence files scripts/notices.mjs already reads (8,771 characters), or decide that the repository's THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is the record and have the header say so.
findings.risk: (a) changes only the first bytes of the release file, so its hash; nothing rendered changes. (b) adds about 9 KB. The OFL and Lucide texts contain '--', which build.mjs:138 refuses inside a comment, so the dashes need rewriting or the texts another container. The texts also contain URLs, so they must sit outside 'page' as the header does, or the no-URL assertion fails.

findings.title: The game has no licence or copyright line of its own
findings.where: /home/user/tech-sales-trail (no LICENSE or COPYING among the 394 tracked files); package.json; README.md:253-257; the built file's header
findings.evidence: The only licence-like tracked files are THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and scripts/notices.mjs. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md:3 says 'The game's own code and writing are not covered by these notices.' package.json has 'private': true and no 'license' or 'author' field. The README's 'Credits and licences' section covers the four bundled works only. The file's header begins 'Tech Sales Trail 2.1.0. One self-contained file' with no copyright line for the game. By default that means all rights reserved: a recipient is invited to download and play (README.md:23) but is told nothing about passing the file on or reusing the code or writing.
findings.proposal: The owner decides, and nobody else should choose for them: either one sentence under 'Credits and licences' in the README saying who holds the copyright and what a recipient may do (for example play and share the unmodified file), or a LICENSE file with an open licence for the code. Leaving it as it is remains a valid choice if 'all rights reserved' is intended.
findings.risk: No technical risk. A licence choice is hard to take back once the file is in other hands, which is why it should be the owner's and not part of an automated polish pass.

findings.title: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md does not name scheduler, which the file's own header lists as bundled
findings.where: scripts/notices.mjs:15 (the React entry of PARTS); THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md (the table)
findings.evidence: The built file's header reads 'react 18.3.1, react-dom 18.3.1, scheduler 0.23.2. Copyright (c) Facebook, Inc. and its affiliates. MIT License.' and the script contains scheduler's code ('unstable_scheduleCallback' occurs 3 times). The table in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md lists 'react 18.3.1, react-dom 18.3.1' only. The omission has no legal substance: the LICENSE files of react, react-dom and scheduler are byte-identical (sha256 52412d7b...cf2bfc85), and that text is reproduced. Nothing else is bundled but unlisted, and nothing is listed but not bundled.
findings.proposal: In scripts/notices.mjs:15 add ', ' + version("scheduler") to the React entry's version string and regenerate the file with node scripts/notices.mjs.
findings.risk: None to the game. The regenerated file must be committed, or the script's --check mode fails.

not_checked: What Chrome or Edge actually sends when the announcer speaks with an online voice: only Chromium exists here and it reports 0 speech voices, so that part of the second finding rests on documented browser behaviour and on voice lists I reconstructed; only the game's choice of voice was observed.
Whether any external URL resolves: none was fetched, as instructed. All are well-formed and none points at something that plainly cannot exist.
Whether the five people named in docs/2.1 are real.

How the public link is served. If GitHub Pages publishes the whole tree, everything tracked is reachable beside index.html, including test/baseline/v1.21/index.html, an old build kept as a test baseline that loads React and Babel from cdnjs.cloudflare.com and fonts from fonts.googleapis.com and still has the account 'Oracle Dumpling'. I could not see the Pages configuration.

Git history beyond pattern scans of file contents. Commit messages and trailers were out of scope. Commit author fields carry the owner's name with a GitHub no-reply address and an AI coding tool's no-reply address; I did not judge whether either should be public.
Trade mark registers for the invented names (clAInk, Shitcorp, Scheisskorp, the account names): judged from general knowledge only.
Firefox and Safari: not available here, so the offline and console results are Chromium's.
Legal sufficiency of the notices: the fourth and fifth findings are a reading of the licence texts, not legal advice.
I did not run the project's own build, verify or lint scripts, as the ground rules require, so the risk notes about them come from reading their source.
